findings.title: LogCapture ships a FOURTH channel it does not name and only half-watches: record.getThrown() is appended as Throwable.toString(), so a signed URL in a CAUSE's message or anywhere in a stack trace is invisible
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING MUTATION (compiles, whole :ingest:test green, 0 failures; DirectServingTest 13/13). Applied in SubscriptionHub.mintGrant on the line immediately after `binjava.binstore.SignedUrl signed = issuer.grantFor(segmentKey);` -- the same insertion point at which four OTHER leak forms all red the suite: `System.getLogger("binjava.ingest.SubscriptionHub").log(System.Logger.Level.WARNING, "signing context", new IllegalStateException("outer", new IllegalStateException(signed.url())));` -- GREEN. CONTROLS, to prove the gap is precisely the cause chain and not a dead probe: at the SAME line, the println form, the {0}-parameter form at INFO, the same at DEBUG, and the supplier form ALL turn theGrantReachesNOLogLine red. The mechanism is LogCapture.java:88-90: `logged.append(record.getThrown())` resolves to String.valueOf(Throwable), which is `getClass().getName() + ": " + getLocalizedMessage()` of the TOP frame only -- no getCause() walk and no stack frames. WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A PREFERENCE, AND WHY IT IS ONLY A MINOR. The class javadoc enumerates exactly three channels, numbers them, and closes with 'All three feed one buffer, so a leak through any of them fails the same assertion' -- while the code appends a fourth, partial one that the javadoc never mentions. That is round 4's own lesson repeated one level down: this file exists because 'a partial probe does not fail -- it reports a clean run', and the getThrown() line is a partial probe inside the instrument written to replace partial probes. It is a MINOR rather than a major for two measured reasons. (i) The residual is already OWNED elsewhere: GrantNeverLoggedTest.java:182-189 states that the cause IS chained deliberately, that a trace therefore prints whatever the backend wrote, that this is the BACKEND's rule-4 defect stated in BinStore.presign's javadoc, and that M5.42 owns checking it once a capable backend exists. So the chained-cause channel is a known gap with a row, not an unnoticed one. (ii) No ONE-LINE production change on the path this row adds reaches the cause channel without also hitting a live one -- the only site in the tree that logs a Throwable is DefaultIngest.pushLoop, and it concatenates e.getMessage() into the message text, which channel 2 reads; mintGrant's own UncheckedIOException message is `"segment " + segmentKey + " could not be signed for delivery"` and cannot hold a URL, since the URL does not exist on that branch. THE CHEAP CLOSE, if it is taken at all, is to walk the cause chain and append the frames -- `for (Throwable t = record.getThrown(); t != null; t = t.getCause()) logged.append(t).append('\n');` -- or, if the chained-cause residual is deliberately out of scope, to SAY SO in the javadoc beside the other three channels rather than leaving the code and the prose disagreeing about how many channels there are. Per review.md rule 11 fixing a minor is permitted and usually wrong; the prose half is the part that costs nothing to get right.

findings.title: r4-t2's structural half is unfixed: the presign javadoc was REWRITTEN in place and is still dangling, so presign now carries no doc comment at all
findings.failure_scenario: NO SURVIVING MUTATION IS CLAIMED; this is the half of an earlier finding that the fix did not answer, reported because leaving it silently closed is how a finding gets lost. r4-t2 named two defects: a stale paragraph AND the block being orphaned by the two new fields. The stale paragraph was rewritten and is now true (verified above). The ORPHANING is byte-for-byte unchanged: StoreFakes.java:258-287 is the long presign doc comment, line 287 is its close, 288 is a SECOND doc comment `/** When set, every presign throws it ... */`, 289 is the field `java.io.IOException failSigningWith;`, and the presign method itself is at line 295 with NO doc comment above it. Java binds a doc comment to the immediately following declaration, so the one-liner documents the field and the long block is a dangling comment attached to nothing -- it no longer appears on presign in any rendered javadoc, and a reader who opens presign sees only the two inline comments inside its body, neither of which mentions the EPOCH trap. The failure this invites is the one the block's own closing sentence names: 'A later author reading "unconstrained" would edit exactly what these paragraphs exist to protect' -- except the paragraphs are now not where that author will be looking. The fix is a move, not a rewrite: put the block back immediately above the presign signature at line 295 and leave the two field comments where they are. Minor, non-blocking, and per review.md rule 11 the round's surface is the prose a fix would add, so this is stated for the commit body rather than demanded.
